messages:
emma-partners: Heads up  NimbusAI dropped a model bundle (Nimbus-Large-v1) and their LICENSE.txt says 'non-commercial research only'. They also attached a hardware-accel binary built for their partner appliance (EdgeAccel). We need to map acceptable partner lanes: cloud marketplace listing, hosted API, Dedicated, SI installs.
rory-legal: Research-only prevents commercial resell/marketplace listing. We can negotiate a focused Distribution License (DL) that permits hosting and delivery of compiled runtime artifacts while keeping raw checkpoints restricted. Also need explicit appliance binary redistribution terms.
jamal-eng: Technicals: bundle includes FP32 checkpoints, tokenizer, and a precompiled EdgeAccel kernel binary (ARM64) plus source for conversion script. The kernel is tied to EdgeAccel SDK v2. If they won't provide source, we need a redistributable kernel binary with an ABI guarantee and checksum. Without that we can't support SI installs on generic infra.
mei-ops: Ops note: their artifact bucket gives read access tied to NimbusCI role. Do NOT accept cross-account roles. Ask for presigned, time-limited downloads and a signed manifest (SHA256) per file. For marketplace, we require reproducible build steps and provenance.
lucy-ml: From an evaluation perspective: request a small canonical eval set (100 prompts), baseline outputs, and recommended quantization configs. Also request a perf profile on EdgeAccel and on commodity GPUs (throughput, mem/prefix). We need that for model cards and Optimize recommendations.
rob-marketing: Marketing wants to plan a joint launch with Nimbus in 3 weeks. Can we promise a marketplace tile if legal + eng agree? We need packaging and approved copy. Also NSR on attribution requirements.
emma-partners: Rory  what's the minimum acceptable DL clause to permit a Marketplace tile and hosted API while protecting Nimbus' IP and avoiding raw checkpoint distribution?
rory-legal: Minimal terms: 1) Grant Redwood a non-exclusive, worldwide, sublicensable license to host, serve, and distribute compiled/quantized runtime artifacts (containers, binaries). 2) Prohibit redistribution of raw checkpoints. 3) Require signed manifest (SHA256) and provenance for each release. 4) Require disclosure of appliance-specific binaries and whether redistribution is permitted; if allowed, provide redistributable binary with checksum. 5) Supplier to certify export/compliance and list any geo-restrictions. Add SI-onprem clause: SI transfers need a per-customer addendum + KYC.
jamal-eng: Add to that: we need kernel ABI stability commitment or versioned redistributable binaries, a compatibility matrix (max context, tokenization rules), and smoke test scripts. For appliance lane, we need to know whether the EdgeAccel kernel supports FP16/INT8 and the kv-cache semantics.
mei-ops: For SI lane: if Nimbus refuses raw checkpoints, propose an 'installer image' approach: Redwood builds a sealed runtime image (with their redistributable binaries) and we distribute to SI under contract. Need their written permission and logging/audit hooks. Also require signed SHA256 manifest and GPG-signed provenance.
lucy-ml: Also ask for a minimal 'regression bundle' (5-10 prompts with expected outputs) that we can use to detect quality regressions across quantization.
rob-marketing: If we can secure a hosting grant and manifest this week, Marketing can draft joint copy and hold a co-announcement in 3 weeks. If more legal back-and-forth required, timeline slips. Please flag ASAP.
emma-partners: Actionables: Ben? (typo) actually, I'll reach out. Planned outreach: 1) propose two lanes in email: Marketplace/Hosted (DL + manifest + redistributable kernel if needed) and SI/Dedicated (DL + SOW + per-customer addendum). 2) Include Rory's starter clause and checklist for them to fill.
ci-bot: created TICKET PARTNERS-552: "NimbusAI distribution license + appliance binary terms"  assignee: emma-partners.

emma-partners: I'll paste a short starter clause for the email: "Supplier grants Redwood a non-exclusive, worldwide, sublicensable license to host, serve, and distribute compiled runtime artifacts (containers, quantized binaries) to Redwood customers. Redistribution of raw checkpoints is prohibited. Supplier must provide a signed manifest (SHA256), provenance build steps, and disclose any appliance-specific binaries with redistribution permissions. SI/on-prem transfers require an executed SOW and per-customer addendum. Supplier will declare export controls and any geo-restrictions."

rory-legal: Also add: "Supplier must provide either kernel source or a redistributable binary with checksum and a stable ABI guarantee; absent that, Redwood will only offer hosted endpoints on Redwood-managed infra and will not support raw weight transfers to third parties."

jamal-eng: I'll prepare a short technical checklist to include: manifest, provenance, kernel source/binary & checksum, compatibility matrix (context len, tokenizer norms), eval/regression set, perf profile on EdgeAccel + commodity GPUs.

mei-ops: I'll prepare ops requirements: presigned artifact URLs, object locking off until verification, audit logs for SI installs, and GPG-signed manifests.

emma-partners: Sending draft now. Post NimbusAI's response here. We need legal+eng signoff within 10 business days to keep marketing timeline.
